Treatment Summary
The patient presented after a collision in which another vehicle struck the patient's car while the patient was turning left. The
patient repotred neck pain and stiffness beginning shortly after the impact, consistent with a whiplash-type mechanism for a crash
of this kind. Over three visits, the patient was managed with a standard cousre of conservative care, including range-of-motion
exercises, the use of a cervical collar for a short period, and as-needed anti-inflammatory medication. Examination findings
included reduced cervical range of motion and tenderness over the paraspinal muscles, which support the reported injury.
Neurological screening and imaging-related assessments were within normal limits. The patient reported no prior injury to the
neck or upper back. Symptoms improved steadily, and care was tapered and then discontinued as the patient's function returned
toward baseline. Two charges with similar service descriptions submitted on the same day are currently under review by the
billing office.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
